Fwiw, here is the best I can discern what happened:

1. Trump announces a ceasefire plan, saying Iran has a 10 point plan that is a reasonable basis for negotiations.
2. Iran releases that 10 point plan, which includes no more incursions in Lebanon (#10, screenshotted above)
3. Huge blowback to the plan released, with framing that it's a terrible deal for the U.S.
4. The U.S. says "no not that plan - that was the original plan but we negotiated a new 10 point plan," essentially affirming the exi

It's literally #10 in the plan that Trump posted and the admin circulated? I'm looking right at it.




Aaron Rupar (@atrupar)

JD Vance: "I think this comes from a legitimate misunderstanding. I think the Iranians thought the ceasefire included Lebanon, and it just didn't. We never made that promise, we never indicated that was gonna be the case."

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/atrupar/status/2041963943753548041#m

The ceasefire is basically over. In fact, it never really began. But Trump got the headlines he wanted from all across the media space, all born from some social media posts and zero action or details

NEWS: Anthropic's new model, Claude Mythos, is so powerful that it is not releasing it to the public. 

Instead, it is starting a 40-company coalition, Project Glasswing, to allow cybersecurity defenders a head start in locking down critical software.

This framing resonates with me. But what's the best counter-framing? 

Before Trump's war, _____________________?


Travis Akers 🇺🇸 (@travisakers)

Before Trump’s war the Strait of Hormuz was open, sanctions were in place, and gas was $2.39.

Now Iran controls the Strait, sanctions will be lifted, gas is $4.99, 13 Americans are dead, over 300 injured, and the loss of hundreds of billions in aircraft and U.S. base repairs.



— https://nitter.net/travisakers/status/2041688433320432050#m

This is important. It's ridiculous to pretend Iran got some unambiguous win; they took huge losses, are absolutely weakened, and the country is going to be in a fractured, confused state for sometime. It's *also* true that they may end up economically stronger w/ proof of concept for a new way to exact leverage against the world, which is not good. A decidedly mixed bag.


David Harsanyi (@davidharsanyi)
